title: Multi-source reconstruction: multiple conversation-log folders + multiple file-history folders feeding one file's history (in service of task 83)
description:
The jot codebase's revision history — THE reconstruction this whole tool exists for (task 83) — is scattered across at least four conversation-log sources (the original jot project's folder in ~/.claude/projects, the jot-recovery project's folder, this RevEng project, and one or two other projects whose sessions edited the jot plugin from other cwds) and at least two file-history snapshot locations (some under jot-recovery, some under the original jot project's .claude location). Today one reconstruction takes ONE projects folder + ONE file-history dir. Three parts, in this order:
(1) FILE IDENTITY ACROSS SOURCES (investigate FIRST — parts 2 and 3 are only as correct as this answer): how to establish that records/snapshots from different sources refer to the SAME file when sessions ran under different roots (~/Programming/jot vs ~/Programming/jot-recovery vs other cwds) — absolute paths won't match; identity likely = root-relative path agreement (the task-137 repo-matching rule) + content agreement; decide how each source declares its root (per-source cwd remap config, extending the s87 cwd-remap mechanism).
(2) MULTI-SOURCE INPUTS: engine accepts multiple conversation-log folders and multiple file-history snapshot folders for a single reconstruction. Existing seams to extend, not a rewrite: buildProjectReconstruction already merges a LIST of JSONL paths (jfred/src/viewer_api.ts:56 — today all from one folder); snapshots already arrive via the injectable BackupReader (file-history sidecar is a second input; cross-session @vN blob reads already resolve to the OWNING session); config shape probably reveng-paths.json growing source lists.
(3) MERGED PER-FILE RECONSTRUCTION: define how one file's revision timeline is built when its events come from several session logs and snapshots from several folders — cross-source interleaving by timestamp (wall-clock skew between machines/sessions?), what wins when sources disagree, and how branch/rewind structure from different logs composes.
(4) NEW SCENARIO REQUIRED: create a new scenario that covers what is being built — a multi-source capture (run via /run-scenario like the sNN suite) where MULTIPLE files are edited across MULTIPLE sessions run from different project roots, producing multiple conversation-log folders and multiple file-history snapshot folders, with ground-truth revision ladders spanning the sources (cross-source interleaves and root-relative identity matches across differing absolute paths). Coverage bar: exercise essentially everything scenario s87 exercises — the newer-CC wire format and its four mechanisms (cwd remap, time-aware indirection, result-instant rename stamping, git-INDEX staged-blob evidence) — just split up across the multiple sessions. The scenario joins the executed sweep and becomes the acceptance gate for parts 1-3.
(4a) RUN-SCENARIO TOOLING PREREQUISITE: today /run-scenario (jfredToolsPlugin:run-scenario) executes each scenario in a random temp directory — a multi-session scenario needs the ability to SPECIFY where the modifications happen (named/fixed workspace roots reused across the scenario's sessions), so add that capability to the run-scenario skill + scripts first.
Scope note: this is engine-architecture work — plan it (design doc first) before touching code; the 87-scenario sweep must stay green since single-source is the degenerate case.
